newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Westpac says financial services profit up.
newsitem.headline: Westpac says financial services profit up.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corp said on Monday its Westpac Financial Services Group reported a net profit of A$38.2 million for the six months to March 31, a 115 percent improved on the corresponding period last year.
Westpac said the increased profit was boosted by a strong level of sales with A$1.5 billion of retail products sold through Westpac's advisor and planner networks in the March half.
Total funds under management is now above A$13 billion, an increase of over 25 percent over the previous half.
Westpac's financial services group comprises its funds management, insurance and superannuation operations.
Westpac last week announced a 12.9 percent rise in net profit to A$638 million for the half year.
Westpac Financial Services (WFS) managing director David Fite said in a statement its custody business and general insurances business continued to perform well.

"WFS continues to lead the custody market with assets under administration increasing 16 percent to A$72.9 billion in the first half of the year," he said. General insurance premiums increased eight percent over the previous six months to A$60
million, reflecting strong growth across a range of products.
